svg.title: Contract holder, billable party and payer
svg.text: Sets how a procedure is priced and what
Holds the invoice email, never the Contract.
a reference record, or the Booking
Who pays if the holder doesn't
Every Booking names one. Prefilled from the
patient; the office or anaesthetist can change it.
A holder can be billed or not: it is a setting
on each holder, not fixed by its kind.
The patient is the person treated (one record
per NHI). They are billed only as the payer.
A payer under 18 is a mild warning, not a block.
The office's main job at booking setup is to identify who pays.
Is the holder the billable party?
A setting on the holder, carried by every Contract it holds.
a hospital, or an insurer that
One invoice per billable party on the Booking. Splitting one fee
between two payers is an action on the Booking, not the Contract.
There are no kinds of Contract: the holder's setting decides who is billed.
AA holds No contract (RVG) and is never billed,
so it bills the payer. Insured patients who claim
the money back themselves are billed under it.
A code such as SXAP from the rooms or the
hospital says the hospital is arranging cover
Contract holder: who the deal is with·Billable party: who gets the invoice·Payer: on the Booking, billed when the holder is not
